subject: Post-demo: Connectivity & integration playbook — VPC endpoints, auth, embeddings
messages:
From: Rachel Simmons <rachel.simmons@finlytics.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinLytics Platform Team <platform@finlytics.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Thanks — quick recap + connectivity questions

Hi Nikhil — thanks for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can scope network and security with our infra team:

Summary of needs from FinLytics
- Low-latency chat generation for internal analyst UI (~50–150ms p50 target)
- Embeddings index for semantic search + a reranker pipeline (batch + near-realtime)
- Support for structured tool-calling responses (we’ll call back to an orchestration service)

Networking & connectivity items we need clarity on
1) Private connectivity: we prefer private egress from our VPC to Redwood rather than opening public egress. Do you support VPC endpoints or private peering?
2) IP allowlists: we need your egress IP ranges or a mechanism that doesn’t rely on IPs changing frequently.
3) mTLS: Can you support mutual TLS for API traffic from our side (client certs) in addition to API keys?
4) DNS / egress: If traffic leaves via our NAT, are there any DNS SRV/CNAME requirements?
5) SDK/auth: For initial integration we’ll use your JavaScript SDK. Does the SDK support cert-based auth or only token-based? What’s the recommended pattern for rotating credentials?

Attachments: I attached a rough network diagram and our vendor questionnaire.

Next steps: Can you send a short integration playbook we can share with infra/security? Also propose a 30–45m technical call with infra + platform.

Thanks,
Rachel Simmons
Head of Platform Integrations
FinLytics

[attachment: finlytics-proposed-network-diagram.png] [attachment: finlytics-vendor-questionnaire.pdf]

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Simmons <rachel.simmons@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick recap + connectivity questions

Hi Rachel — great to meet you and the FinLytics team. Appreciate the clear notes — below is a short playbook and proposed next steps. I’ve looped in Monica (network/infra) and Aditya (SDK & auth).

Short answers up front
- Private connectivity: We support both VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink-style) for hosted customers and VPC peering for Redwood Private deployments. For hosted customers we can also provide a stable set of egress IPs as a fallback.
- IP allowlists: We publish a weekly stable CIDR bundle for customers and offer a signed JWKS + hostname verification path if you prefer DNS-based allowlisting.
- mTLS: Supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted (Redwood API) we can enable mutual TLS per-customer via managed client certificates (requires an enterprise add-on).
- SDK/auth: SDKs are token-first; we have hooks in the SDK for certificate pinning and custom transport if you want mTLS at the SDK level. We recommend short-lived tokens rotated via your KMS + a service account.

Proposed next steps
1) Tech call (30–45m) this week — Monica will drive network specifics, Aditya will cover SDK/auth and structured output patterns.
2) Share a one-page integration checklist (attached) + the CIDR bundle if you choose IP allowlist.
3) If you prefer private peering, we’ll provide a connectivity workbook and an internal timeline.

If that sounds good I’ll schedule a call and send the playbook + checklist you can share with infra.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

[attachment: redwood-integration-checklist.pdf]

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: FinLytics connectivity — requested items for the tech call

Monica / Aditya — forwarding FinLytics notes. They want private connectivity + mTLS options and will run this through security. Please see below and advise what we should put in the playbook. Key asks I want covered on the call:

Action items for call (Monica)- Confirm whether hosted PrivateLink is available in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 and lead time for enabling it per-customer.
- Provide the current stable CIDR bundle and explain update cadence and rollover process.
- Confirm whether we can accept incoming client mTLS certs (customer presented) on the hosted API or whether that requires Private deployment. If hosted we may need to generate per-customer certs and provide cert rotation docs.
- Clarify DNS/eDNS expectations: do we require customers to resolve any internal service hostnames or is public DNS sufficient? Any special CNAMEs?

Action items for call (Aditya)- SDK: doc the recommended auth flow (short-lived token via service account) and sample for cert-based transport if possible.
- Structured output / tool-calling: propose a minimal schema for tool responses FinLytics can implement and an example reranker flow (embeddings -> candidate retrieval -> rerank).
- Embeddings: sample throughput and suggestions for batching and caching for a 10M-embedding index (initial warm-up).

Notes to include in playbook- Example curl + SDK snippets for: token creation, token rotation, example of cert-backed transport.
- Failover: how we fall back to a compatible model variant or degrade to public API under burst.

I’ll consolidate answers into the playbook and send to Rachel before the call.

Thanks — let me know if anything else belongs on the list.

–Nikhil

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: FinLytics connectivity — requested items for the tech call

Short answers / checklist (we’ll expand during the call)
- PrivateLink / endpoints: Available in us-west-2 today; eu-west-1 on request (~2–3 week lead time for certs & routing updates). We’ll provide the endpoint DNS name and an ARN-based enablement flow.
- CIDR bundle: Attached list is our current published egress ranges (stable, weekly patch window). Recommend customers reference the bundle and optionally allow the JWKS hostname for host-based allowlisting.
- mTLS: Hosted customers can use managed mTLS (enterprise add-on). For customer-presented certificates we need a short onboarding (CSR + metadata); full mutual TLS for Dedicated/Private is supported out-of-the-box.
- DNS / egress: Public DNS is sufficient for most flows. If you enable VPC endpoints we will provide private DNS entries to resolve the endpoint within the customer VPC. No special SRV records required.
- Outbound traffic: If traffic egresses via customer NAT, ensure outbound to our published CIDRs and SNI hostnames: api.redwood-inference.internal and embeddings.redwood-inference.internal.

Aditya — I’ll share the CIDR list and the endpoint provisioning worksheet. Aditya — can you drop the SDK sample link and a short snippet we can include in the playbook?

Monica Patel
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
